hypothesis: An acquired UVM control-file pin remains bound to the original struct file after its numeric FD is closed and reused; a later pin resolves the replacement file independently.
limitations: The host fixture models Linux file references; it is not a live kernel race test.
No GPU, NVIDIA module, CUDA process, UVM runtime, or hardware behavior was exercised.
The test covers close and reuse after the pin has acquired fget; it does not claim to define concurrent close/reuse semantics before the kernel resolves the FD.

scenario.first_pin_backend_memory: original backend handle recorded before FD reuse
scenario.observed: the original pin retained the original file reference until unpin; the reused FD selected the replacement file and its distinct backend handle; both RM frees were blocked while pinned and succeeded for the exact backend objects after unpin
